html:
Lynden Pindling was the first Black premier and the first prime minister of the Bahamas. He led the country to majority rule in 1967 and to independence on 10 July 1973.

Until then a white merchant elite, the Bay Street Boys, ran the colony, though most people were Black. Pindling's Progressive Liberal Party won the 1967 election by a narrow margin, which Bahamians remember as Majority Rule Day.

He governed for 25 years, expanding schools and tourism. His later years were clouded by charges of corruption and of ties to drug smugglers, and he lost power in 1992. He is called the father of the nation of the Bahamas, the heir of the Loyalist era's enslaved majority, and a leader of the Commonwealth Caribbean.
sum: Lynden Pindling was the first Black premier and the first prime minister of the Bahamas. He led the country to majority rule in 1967 and to independence on 10 July 1973.
